children: Gold futures fell to their lowest level in two-and-a-half months, and silver sank to its worst settlement since November on ‌Thursday as higher oil prices prompted inflation concerns and the potential for higher interest rates.
Brent crude surged 4% to its highest in nearly six months after Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia sparked concerns of further disruption to Middle East energy supplies.

Gold has also been under pressure as higher yields and a strong U.S. dollar reduce the attraction of holding non-yielding assets such as precious metals, although gold's losses have been moderated by central bank buying and strong demand for gold ETFs.

"We believe the latest weakness reflects mounting pressure from rising U.S. Treasury yields, a stronger dollar, and renewed inflation concerns as Brent crude climbs above $110/bbl," Zaye Capital Markets chief investment officer Naeem Aslam said in a note.

Also, U.S. consumer and producer inflation data last week came in hotter than expected, ‌strengthening ⁠the case for tighter policy, even though most followers expect Federal Reserve officials will not raise rates when they meet on October 27-28, opting instead to make a move in December.

Silver faces additional pressure because its use in industrial applications exposes prices to weaker manufacturing activity, Aslam said, adding that silver's price direction will depend on whether improving industrial demand and supply constraints can overcome pressure from restrictive U.S. monetary policy.
